note:
Seeded at 1678. The Python half of the `--addon mail` pair: `js_function_length.py --addon mail` has been floored as `jsfunclen_mail` since 2026-07, but its Python counterpart was never wired -- `py_function_length.py --addon mail` printed a `ratchet.py pyfunclen_mail --count` command for a baseline that did not exist, so Python function length in `addons/mail` was measured by nothing. `pyfunclen` measures `odoo/`, the core package, and none of its 120 entries is under `addons/`.

Excess lines above the 80-line budget, not the count of offenders -- same metric as `pyfunclen`, for the same reason: splitting one long function into several merely-long ones raises the count while lowering the excess.

Three measurements, because the number moved twice in two commits and only one of them was a structural change:

    0fc9ec65d44  1708
    6dd3d3a3026  1725   <- +17, the parameter-typing sweep
    d4a96315ce1  1678   <- -47, mail.message.create split

The +17 is worth naming: 6dd3d3a3026 added no logic at all, and annotating a signature makes ruff format break it across lines, so every typed parameter list that no longer fits on one line grows the function it heads. This gate therefore moves with a typing pass as well as with an extraction -- the same non-monotonicity `jsfunclen_mail`'s note records from a comment strip.

The -47 is `mail.message.create`, 139 lines -> 46: the base64-to-attachment substitution, the attachment access check and the tracking-value commands moved to `_extract_body_attachments`, `_check_created_attachments_access` and `_create_tracking_values`, and the reply-to resolution to `_get_reply_to_batch`. That also took `create` out of the `c901_addons` set (25 > 20).

The tree's shape at seeding: 50 functions over 80 lines, longest `mail_thread.message_route` at 278, then `_prepare_mail_values_dynamic` 190 and `message_post` / `_message_notify_batch` at 167 each. Those four are 40% of the excess; this number moves when they do.

Command: python tooling/architecture/py_function_length.py --addon mail --count
